summary.name: Hosted Graphite incident postmortem template
summary.one_liner: A blog post in which Hosted Graphite shares its internal SRE incident postmortem template, with guidance on the review process and what to write in each section.
keywords: what went well what went badly
use_cases: Running a postmortem review with SRE sign-off
Turning incident lessons into tracked follow-up tickets
Preparing postmortem content for a status page
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Hosted Graphite's postmortem template, which has sections for Summary, Background, What happened, What went well, What went badly, and What are we going to do in the future. It recommends writing in two passes: a content and accuracy draft first, then a separate language and tone pass for public documents. It says first drafts should get sign-off from at least two SREs, and that the final version can be pasted into Statuspage after formatting checks. Each follow-up action should link to an open ticket, and the page suggests a list of further reading on incident review.
notable: Two-step writing process that separates content review from language and tone review
Each planned follow-up action must have an open ticket referenced in the document
Asks authors to record the specific information available when each action was taken
caveats: The template is a simple structure, and the page says it prioritises process and content over format
Public postmortems are written in the same tone as status page communications
